geometry.locator: arXiv:1003.1391 Table 1.2 (per-reactor near/far baselines); OSM reactor-building positions
geometry.note: Nonlinear least-squares multilateration (scipy.optimize.least_squares on raw Euclidean centre-to-centre distance residuals, local equirectangular projection) of this detector hall's position from the six Hanbit reactor-core buildings (geometry:hanbit-core-r1..r6; accuracy_m 8 each), using the per-reactor near/far distances published in the RENO proposal (arXiv:1003.1391, Table 1.2, 'Distances of the reactor cores from the near and far detectors'). Of all 6! possible assignments of the table's R1-R6 labels to the six OSM buildings (and the reflection of the whole line), only the natural southwest-to-northeast geographic numbering converges to a good fit (residual root-mean-square 3-5 m on baselines of 300-1560 m, i.e. well under 2%); every other assignment leaves a residual of hundreds of metres, so this numbering (not independently sourced -- the proposal gives no reactor coordinates) is adopted on that self-consistency alone. accuracy_m is set above the fit residual to also cover the OSM buildings' own ~8 m footprint accuracy and this table being the experiment's 2010 design/proposal figure rather than an as-built survey (the collaboration's own later papers confirm the same overall geometry only as flux-weighted averages: 294 m / 1383 m from the array centre, arXiv:1204.0626).

method: Nonlinear least-squares multilateration (scipy.optimize.least_squares on raw Euclidean centre-to-centre distance residuals, local equirectangular projection) of this detector hall's position from the six Hanbit reactor-core buildings (geometry:hanbit-core-r1..r6; accuracy_m 8 each), using the per-reactor near/far distances published in the RENO proposal (arXiv:1003.1391, Table 1.2, 'Distances of the reactor cores from the near and far detectors'). Of all 6! possible assignments of the table's R1-R6 labels to the six OSM buildings (and the reflection of the whole line), only the natural southwest-to-northeast geographic numbering converges to a good fit (residual root-mean-square 3-5 m on baselines of 300-1560 m, i.e. well under 2%); every other assignment leaves a residual of hundreds of metres, so this numbering (not independently sourced -- the proposal gives no reactor coordinates) is adopted on that self-consistency alone. accuracy_m is set above the fit residual to also cover the OSM buildings' own ~8 m footprint accuracy and this table being the experiment's 2010 design/proposal figure rather than an as-built survey (the collaboration's own later papers confirm the same overall geometry only as flux-weighted averages: 294 m / 1383 m from the array centre, arXiv:1204.0626).
name: RENO near detector hall position (derived point)
notes: Checks against units 3–6 sit 3.3–3.8 % (10–28 m) from the TDR distances; over 300–740 m baselines that is the expected size of the offset between a reactor-building centroid and the core centre, so the tolerance is 5 % and accuracy_m 30 m rather than the fit residual alone.
The shape is derived from or copied from OpenStreetMap data (src:geo-reactors-osm-hanbit-reactors), which makes it a derivative database under the ODbL regardless of the derivation step in between.

summary.plain: RENO near detector hall, positioned by trilateration from the RENO proposal's published reactor-to-detector distances and the reactor buildings' OpenStreetMap positions.
